question: How does oWALNUTS Sampler::run wall time scale with chains in {1,2,4,8,16} and threads in {1,2,4,8,16} on (a) a cheap hand-written target, (b) a medium Rust autodiff target and (c) a BridgeStan target on this 16-core Windows machine, and where scaling is sub-linear, why (allocator, shared counters / false sharing, RNG, thread spawn, per-transition result collection, BridgeStan serialisation, hybrid cores, load imbalance, machine contention)?
api_under_test: owalnuts::sampler::Sampler::new().warmup(W).draws(D).chains(C).seed(S).threads(T).run(&target, &uniform_starts(target, C, S, 2.0, 100)); every other setting at the 0.2.0 defaults (Tuning::default, Metric::diagonal, Adaptation::default, Limits::default = admit_worst_case, cached initial evaluation). Wall = Instant around Sampler::run only (start search excluded).
driver_facts_from_code_reading: sample_chains_validated clamps threads to min(threads, chains) and runs one Rayon par_iter item per chain in a run-local scoped pool built per run; threads > chains cells are therefore duplicates of threads = chains

Limits::default() has admit_worst_case = true, so the default Sampler::run creates a TargetEvaluationBudget of exactly the worst case and wraps the target in BudgetedTarget, whose reserve() is a fetch_update compare-and-swap on ONE shared AtomicUsize per target call across all chain threads
per-chain RNG is a private SmallRng; per-chain samples/diagnostics are reserved up front; kernel workspaces are thread-local caches
on Windows ReplicatedStanTarget always has one effective owned worker and a process-global native-call mutex (BRIDGESTAN-OWNED-WORKER-V1), so BridgeStan calls are serialised by construction

ll1000.label: (b) medium Rust autodiff
ll1000.what: owalnuts-autodiff AutodiffTarget<LocalLevel{T=1000, normalised=false}> on LocalLevelData::simulate(1000, 2026083101) (the autodiff benchmark's T=1000 path)

ark.label: (c) BridgeStan
ark.what: posteriordb 28f8d3d arK-arK compiled with BridgeStan 2.9.0 (no STAN_THREADS, mingw32-make), ReplicatedStanTarget::load(.., replicas = 16) -> one effective owned worker on Windows

seeds_note: 945101-945103 verified absent from every tracked file as a standalone number (git grep with digit/decimal guards); calibration used 945199 (non-evidence)
calibration_before_freeze: Non-evidence seed 945199, used only to size the workloads and to check the instruments: gauss100 1000/4000 took 0.066 s at C=T=1 (raised to 20,000 draws, 0.26-0.28 s); ll1000 300/300 took 9.2 s at C=T=1 and one C=T=4 run took 161.7 s wall with 41 s CPU while the machine was 87 % busy (a starvation episode; reduced to 200/200); ark 1000/1000 2.5 s at C=T=1 and 7.8 s at C=T=4 (reduced to 500/500). The calibration timeline probe on gauss100 measured ~1.7-2.0 us per gradient outside the user target (kernel + driver + wrappers) against ~0.09 us inside it, and ~3 heap allocations per gradient (22 per transition); on ll1000 ~10 us per gradient, 0.024 allocations per gradient, and max/mean chain gradient count 1.44 at C=4. A two-repetition allocator ablation at C=T=16 was within noise. These numbers informed the predictions below.

grid.order: gauss100 then ll1000 then ark; within a target rep-major, chains ascending, threads ascending; strictly sequential, one process per target
grid.cells_note: full = all 25 (C,T); lower = the 15 cells with T <= C (T > C is clamped by the driver; the gauss100 full grid verifies that)
grid.binary: bin/baseline/grid.exe (library at 3583d130, system allocator, no instrumentation)
grid.recorded_per_cell: wall, process user/kernel CPU (GetProcessTimes), system busy core-seconds (GetSystemTimes; other load = system busy - own CPU), page faults, peak working set, gradients per chain, retained divergences, metadata thread_count, draw/work/metadata fingerprints per chain, min bulk ESS (owalnuts::diagnostics::ess_bulk over all chains, min over coordinates), ESS/s, ESS/gradient

bit_identity_check: At fixed (target, chains, seed) the FNV-1a fingerprint of every chain's draws (f64 bits) plus its transition diagnostics and telemetry (Debug text) must be identical across all thread counts and repetitions; the harness records and exits nonzero on any mismatch. Metadata fingerprints are expected to differ across thread counts only through thread_count.

profile.binary: bin/baseline/profile.exe (same library; instrumented global allocator with per-thread padded counters keyed by OS thread id; optional probing target wrapper)
profile.timeline_instrument: per OS thread: calls, TSC cycles inside the user target, thread CPU time and wall span sampled every 256 calls, logical processor sampled every 256 calls and classed P / E / LPE from GetSystemCpuSetInformation (EfficiencyClass, last-level cache). 'Outside' time contains the kernel, driver and the sampler's BudgetedTarget wrapper (the probe sits inside it).
profile.alloc_ablation: system allocator vs a thread-local size-class free-list cache (<= 4 KiB, depth 256) in front of it, ABBA order
profile.cas_bench: n in {1,2,4,8,16} std threads each doing 1/n of 2,000,000 ops of {0,64,256,1024} dependent FP steps followed by: nothing / the BudgetedTarget::reserve fetch_update on one shared counter / a fetch_add on a private padded counter

fix_under_test.mechanism: The default Sampler path reserves every gradient on one shared atomic (TargetEvaluationBudget::reserve), a cache line written by all chain threads per gradient.
fix_under_test.change: walnutpie::sample_chains_with_target_budget_metered(.., BudgetMetering) (crate-private). The public sample_chains_with_target_budget_and_control keeps BudgetMetering::Always (exact started() contract). Sampler::run on the identity/diagonal path passes UnobservedWhenCovered: its budget is private and never read after the run, so when the preflight's exact worst case <= budget maximum (always true under the default admit_worst_case) the target is called unwrapped. An explicit tighter max_target_evaluations still meters and enforces the cap. Dense, structured and continuation-session paths unchanged.
fix_under_test.bit_identity: draws, transition diagnostics, telemetry and metadata (effective_max_target_evaluations, provenance) unchanged; unit test unmetered_covered_budget_is_bit_identical_to_the_metered_run; kernel fingerprint tests must pass

ab.binaries: bin/baseline/grid.exe vs bin/fixed/grid.exe (identical harness; library at 3583d130 vs the fix commit)
ab.order: after the pilot grid and the profile; for rep r and cell index i the arm order is baseline,fixed when (r+i) is even, else fixed,baseline; one process per cell

decision_rule.text: Merge F1 iff (1) every A/B cell has identical draw+work and metadata fingerprints between baseline and fixed and cargo test passes, (2) on gauss100 the ratio median(baseline wall)/median(fixed wall) over the 3 reps is >= 1.15 at chains=threads=8 or at chains=threads=16, and (3) that ratio is >= 1/1.05 at chains=threads=1 and at chains=threads=4 (no regression beyond 5 %). Otherwise do not merge. Contended-pilot walls decide; the quiet rerun (RUN-QUIET.md) is reported beside them and does not overturn the decision.

predictions.P4_ark_speedup_any_T: between 0.8 and 1.1 at every (C, T); efficiency = speedup/T, so 0.05-0.07 at T=16
predictions.P5_bit_identity: 100 % of cells: fingerprints identical across T and reps at fixed (target, C); A/B identical
predictions.P6_allocations: gauss100 2-4 heap allocations per gradient, ll1000 < 0.05; allocator ablation changes C=T=16 wall by less than 5 % (median of 3)
predictions.P7_hybrid_cores: E-core threads spend 1.2-1.6x the CPU time per gradient of P-core threads; no thread is observed on the two LPE cores for most of a run
predictions.P8_cas_bench: with work comparable to a gauss100 gradient (256-1024 FP steps) the shared CAS costs < 1.5x the no-counter control at n=16; with 0-64 steps it costs >= 3x
predictions.P9_fix_F1: baseline/fixed wall ratio on gauss100: 1.00 at C=T=1 and 4 (+-0.03), 1.03 at C=T=8, 1.08 at C=T=16; decision rule NOT met; ll1000 within +-0.03
predictions.P10_why: sub-linear scaling at 8-16 threads is dominated by machine contention (process CPU/wall well below T), chain-length imbalance (wall tracks the longest chain: max/mean chain gradients 1.2-1.6) and hybrid E-cores; thread spawn, RNG and result collection are negligible (< 2 % of wall); the BridgeStan Windows owned worker removes all parallelism

contention_note: CONTENDED PILOT: ten agents share the 16 cores; walls are upper bounds and are labelled as such. Gradient counts, ESS and fingerprints are machine-independent. The shared brief asks for <= 4 threads per process; this study's task requires 8- and 16-thread cells, which are run once (pilot) and kept short.
failure_policy: failures are results; no cell is rerun or tuned after seeing results; every cell reported
